Author: @javiermedina9080
Content:
I really like the video, the way it sort of balances the aspect of well, the food served, since it is a food channel, with the aspect of an interview. Asking questions not just of the food but also of the individual, their experience and what is it they do and how they do it.

Food wise, I think my favorite part was the Basque cake, mostly cause I am Spanish myself, so I do have a bit of a bias. But in all fairness I genuinely think that Basque cake is the best cream cheese style cake out there. It is smooth, fluffy, creamy, filling but not overly sweet or heavy on the palate, like you feel as though you could go for another slide or two after your first one, and it’s not really difficult to make. Ive made like, 5 in the last 2 years and honestly it is really dam easy to make. There are a few key steps to follow but all in all it is just mixing the ingredients in a bowl, putting the mix in a mould and baking it in the oven, and the ingredients is nothing outlandish ir over the top, cream cheese, a lot of cream cheese granted, heavy cream, eggs, sugar, a pinch of salt, and all purpose flour. Thats it, there ain’t nothing much to it, if your starting baking and you want to make a cake, start with a Basque cake.

Something of note, do that try to use baking flour, or flour specifically for baking, it doesn’t tend to rise as well and the texture can be a bit funny, all purpose flour is the go to.

The marmalade on top is optional though, usually Basque cake in Spain, or as we call it “Tarta de la Viña” is served by itself, though you can add marmalade if you want to, more of a preference in that case.

Jhosua of course made it perfectly, it came out rather well, it looked fluffy, creamy, and with the slightly brunt, almost caramelised crust, 10/10, would inhale the whole cake.
